options: A living thing that makes its own food
A thing that eats dead material
questions.explanation: A producer makes its own food, usually by using sunlight to turn water and carbon dioxide into sugar.
questions.misconception: Producers make their own food; hunters and scavengers are consumers, not producers.

questions.prompt: How do most producers make food?
options: From the heat of the soil
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to make sugar - the plant's food.
questions.misconception: Producers do not eat - they build food from sunlight and simple ingredients.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a producer?
questions.explanation: Grass makes its own food through photosynthesis, so it is a producer. A fox, hawk, and worm all eat other things.
questions.misconception: Producers are plants and algae; anything that eats to survive is a consumer.

questions.prompt: Why do food chains start with producers?
options: They turn sunlight into food everything else can use
questions.explanation: Only producers capture sunlight and turn it into food, so every other link depends on them for energy.
questions.misconception: Producers are first because of what they make, not their size, age, or speed.
